title: Listen to him (Mark 9:1–13)
hook: the transfiguration, and the one instruction from the cloud: listen to him
carry: let it change what you do

segments.voice: Yesterday, Peter stood in the road and heard take up your cross. Your line was lose it to find it. What did you give away, and how did it feel? Day one hundred ninety-five.

Six days later, Mark says, Jesus takes three friends, Peter, James and John, up a high mountain, just the four of them. And up there, he changes in front of them. His clothes turn shining, dazzling white, and Mark, who loves a homely detail, says they were whiter than any laundryman on earth could get them. Then two figures appear beside him, talking with him: Elijah and Moses, great prophets from centuries before. And Peter, bless him, has to say something. It's good for us to be here! Let's build three shelters: one for you, one for Moses, one for Elijah. And Mark adds, gently: "For he wist not what to say; for they were sore afraid." He didn't know what to say, so he said something. We have all been Peter.
screen: `A HIGH MOUNTAIN, JUST FOUR.` → `WHITER THAN ANY LAUNDRY.` → `LET'S BUILD THREE SHELTERS.`

segments.voice: While Peter is still planning construction, a cloud comes down and covers them, and a voice speaks out of it. In the King James Bible: "This is my beloved Son: hear him." That's it. One sentence of introduction, one instruction. Not build. Not explain. Hear him. The Greek word means listen, and in the Bible listening is never just sound in the ears. In Hebrew, the same word covers hearing and obeying. To really listen is to let it change what you do. Notice what the voice doesn't say. It doesn't say listen to Moses and Elijah too. Many Christians read those two as standing for the Law and the Prophets, the whole Hebrew Bible, gathered around Jesus. And then, suddenly, they look around and see no one any more, only Jesus, with them. The cloud is gone. The glow is gone. What's left is an ordinary man on a mountain, and the instruction to listen to him. Mark never names the mountain. Christian tradition since early centuries has pointed to Mount Tabor in Galilee, and others suggest Mount Hermon, much nearer Caesarea Philippi. The text is silent. On the way down he tells them to tell no one until he has risen from the dead, and they puzzle over what rising from the dead could mean. Christians call this the transfiguration, from the Latin for being changed in form. Orthodox Christians hold it especially dear, and Catholic, Anglican and many other churches keep it as a feast on the sixth of August.
screen: `A CLOUD, AND ONE SENTENCE.` · `LISTEN MEANS HEAR AND DO.` · `NO ONE LEFT BUT JESUS.` · `A MOUNTAIN MARK NEVER NAMES.` · then, large: `THIS IS MY BELOVED SON: HEAR HIM.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: be the one who listens. Settle, and breathe. For the next two minutes, don't plan anything, don't fix anything, don't build any shelters. Just listen. First the sounds of the room. Then the sounds beyond it, far away. Then the quiet underneath. If you pray, you can hold the line hear him, and wait, without filling the silence. If a thought wants to talk, let it pass like a cloud. The bell holds the time.
Transfiguration, from Latin for being changed in form: the mountain where Jesus shone before Peter, James and John, and a voice said, listen.
Your line: let it change what you do. Today, in one conversation, listen more than you speak. When you feel the urge to build three shelters, wait. Day one hundred ninety-five.

howItsDone: Many churches celebrate the Transfiguration as a feast, on August 6 in the Catholic, Orthodox and Anglican calendars, and many Protestant churches read the story on the Sunday before Lent; Christians often speak of listening to Jesus through reading the Gospels and in silent prayer.

fork.setup: you're Peter, on the mountain. Jesus is shining, Moses and Elijah are beside him, and you are terrified. what do you do?
options: run down to tell the others.
fork.reveal: Peter offers to build, "for he wist not what to say". the voice from the cloud answers with one word of instruction: hear him.

original.note: Greek: listen, hear (said to more than one person). the word from the cloud in Mark 9:7.

trapdoor: what you thought: a glowing miracle on a mountain.
what it means: the whole vision shrinks to one instruction: listen to him. then only Jesus is left.
what a scholar hears: akouete, listen, like the Hebrew shema, joins hearing and obeying. and Mark never names the mountain.

notes: 'Whiter than any laundryman' paraphrases the KJV 'fuller' (9:3). Confirm.
Moses and Elijah as the Law and the Prophets is a common Christian reading, attributed to 'many Christians'.
Mount Tabor identification is attested from about the 4th century (Cyril of Jerusalem, Jerome); Hermon is a modern scholarly suggestion. The script says 'since early centuries'; confirm.

Feast date: August 6 in Catholic, Orthodox (Julian-calendar churches keep it on their own reckoning) and Anglican calendars; many Protestant lectionaries read it on Transfiguration Sunday before Lent. Confirm.
Mark 9:1 (some standing here shall not taste death) is not discussed; Keeper may want a line.
